transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I suppose… I’m here because once I start worrying, I can’t really turn it off. Even when I’ve made the list, checked things, and done what I can, it just keeps going.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like tension or restlessness when you're worrying?
Yes… some. I get kind of wound up, even just sitting at home. I’ll catch myself tapping my fingers on the phone, or getting up to straighten something because sitting still feels… uncomfortable.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?
Yes… it’s mostly worry that keeps circling back. I’ll tell myself I’ve already made the list, checked the dates, done what I can, but my mind doesn’t really let it go.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to suppress or ignore?

I don’t know if I’d call them intrusive exactly… it’s more that the worry just keeps coming back. I try to put it out of my mind because I’ve already checked things and done what I can, but it doesn’t really switch off.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or situations because of your worries?

A little, yes. I still go to my book club and keep up with the garden… but with the exhibition planning, I’ve been taking on less. I’ve turned down a few parts of it because it just feels harder to manage than it used to.
Do you have thoughts that are recurring and difficult to control, which are not just about worry?
Not really, no. I mean… I can’t think of anything like that. It’s mostly just the worrying, as far as I’ve noticed.
Are there any situations or activities that you avoid because you fear something bad might happen?

Not exactly because I think something terrible will happen… it’s more that some things feel like too much now. I still do the garden and go to book club, but I’m less prepared sometimes. And with the exhibition planning, I’ve turned down parts of it because it just feels harder to manage.
Do you have thoughts that are not about worry, but keep coming back to you?
I don’t think so. Nothing separate from the worrying really comes to mind.
Do you have thoughts that are not worries, but keep repeating in your mind?
No… I don’t think so. Not in that way. It’s really just worries, as far as I can tell.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t have… rituals or anything like that, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you have thoughts that are not about worry, but are unwanted and persist in your mind?
Not really… I mean, I have worries that stick around, but I wouldn’t say there are other unwanted thoughts like that.
Are your worries generally about one area of your life, like work or relationships, or are they more about everyday things and tasks?

It’s more spread out, I think. Not just one thing. My mind sort of jumps from the exhibition schedule, to my daughter’s travel plans, to whether the gutters need fixing… little things start to feel like they could turn into something bigger.
Are most of your worries about everyday tasks and responsibilities?

Yes… mostly ordinary responsibilities. It’s things like the exhibition schedule, my daughter’s travel plans, the gutters at the house. They’re small things, but my mind keeps turning them over like they could become much bigger.
Are your worries usually about things that need to be done or taken care of on a daily or weekly basis?

Yes… usually things that need handling. The exhibition schedule, my daughter’s travel plans, the gutters at the house… my mind just goes from one to the next, and they start to feel bigger than they probably are.
Do you have any thoughts that are not worries, but feel like they must be thought about or repeated?
I don’t think so… not like something I have to repeat. It’s more that I get stuck worrying, but I wouldn’t say they’re thoughts that must be thought in that way.
Do you think your worries are worse than what most people would worry about in the same situations?

Yes… I think so. Other people would probably just make a note and deal with it, but my mind keeps roaming from the exhibition schedule to my daughter’s travel plans to the gutters, and then small things start feeling like they could turn into something much bigger.
Do you have thoughts that are not worries but feel like they are repeating in your mind?
No… I don’t think so. Not repeating thoughts like that, anyway. It’s more just… worries coming back around.
Are your worries mostly about things that might happen in the future?

Yes… mostly. It’s usually about what could go wrong next — the exhibition schedule, my daughter traveling, things with the house like the gutters. Little things start to feel like they might turn into something bigger.
Do you feel like you're worrying more than you should be about these everyday things?

Yes… I suppose I do. My mind just keeps moving from one thing to another — the exhibition schedule, my daughter’s travel, the gutters — and then it starts to feel like any of it could become a much bigger problem.
Are your worries currently interfering with your ability to carry out your daily activities?

A little, yes. I still manage my usual things… the garden, book club. But I’m not as prepared as I used to be, and I’ve been saying no to some of the exhibition planning because it just feels harder to keep on top of.
